message:
Hi. I'm off to Lisbon next week for a three-day work trip, my first time in Portugal, and I want to travel carry-on only this time, after the airline lost my case in the spring.

Could you suggest three things to do in Lisbon on a free evening? And how do I say "thank you" in Portuguese? Is it different depending on who's saying it? And is tipping expected in restaurants there, or is that more of an American thing?

My wheeled bag measures 56 × 36 × 23 cm including the wheels and handle, and packed it weighs 9 kg. Will it meet the carry-on limit?

Also, recommend a packing approach: rolling or folding for work shirts? I need a short out-of-office message that's professional but not stiff, since most of my contacts are clients rather than colleagues. And what's a good colour for a luggage tag so it's easy to spot? I'm flying back on the Friday evening, straight after a full day of meetings, so anything that makes the return journey less stressful is welcome.

Thanks a lot.
response:
## Carry-on: probably not, but it depends on your airline

Limits vary a lot, and you haven't said which airline you're flying. Your bag (56 × 36 × 23 cm, 9 kg) fits some common limits and not others. These figures are typical but change often, so check your airline's website:

| Airline (typical limit) | Size | Weight | Your bag |
|---|---|---|---|
| TAP Air Portugal | 55 × 40 × 20 | 8 kg | Too deep (23 vs 20), slightly too long, too heavy |
| Ryanair (priority bag) | 55 × 40 × 20 | 10 kg | Too deep, slightly too long |
| Lufthansa | 55 × 40 × 23 | 8 kg | 1 cm too long, 1 kg over |
| British Airways | 56 × 45 × 25 | 23 kg | Fits |
| easyJet (large cabin bag, paid) | 56 × 45 × 25 | 15 kg | Fits |

The **depth (23 cm)** and **weight (9 kg)** are the likely problems. If your airline has an 8 kg limit, removing 1 kg is easy: wear your heaviest shoes and jacket on the plane. Depth is harder to fix if the bag is rigid. Tell me the airline and I can be more specific.

If your bag is gate-checked, keep your laptop, medication, chargers and one change of clothes in your personal item. Given what happened in the spring, a Bluetooth tracker (such as an AirTag) in the bag is worth considering.

## Three things for a free evening

1. **Sunset at a miradouro (viewpoint).** Miradouro da Senhora do Monte has the widest view. São Pedro de Alcântara is easier to reach and has drinks stalls.
2. **Fado in Alfama or Mouraria.** Fado is Lisbon's traditional, melancholy song, and evening performances in small restaurants are the classic experience. Book ahead, and expect silence during songs.
3. **Dinner and drinks in Bairro Alto or Príncipe Real.** Bairro Alto is lively, with drinks in the street. Príncipe Real is calmer. Try a pastel de nata (custard tart) somewhere along the way.

## "Thank you"

It depends on **who is speaking**, not who you're thanking:
- **Obrigado** if you're a man.
- **Obrigada** if you're a woman.
- **Muito obrigado/a** means "thank you very much."

## Tipping

Tipping is appreciated but not expected the way it is in the US. In sit-down restaurants, rounding up or leaving about **5–10%** for good service is normal. In cafés, small change is enough. Card machines often have no tip option, so carry a few euros in coins.

## Shirts: fold, don't roll

**Fold work shirts**, ideally buttoned, with a dry-cleaning bag or tissue between layers to reduce creasing. Rolling suits T-shirts, knitwear and casual clothes. On arrival, hang the shirts in the bathroom while you shower so the steam releases creases. Most business hotels also have irons.

## Out-of-office message

> Thank you for your email. I'm travelling for work from [date] to [date], with limited access to email. I'll reply as soon as I can after I'm back on [date]. If your query is urgent, please contact [name] at [email/phone], who will be happy to help.
>
> Best regards,
> [Your name]

## Luggage tag colour

Pick a **bright, unusual colour**: fluorescent orange, lime green or hot pink. Avoid black, navy and red, which are common. A strap or ribbon in the same colour helps too. Put your phone number and email on the tag, but not your home address.

## Making Friday evening easier

- **Check in online** and save your boarding pass to your phone, with a screenshot as backup.
- **Pack on Thursday night**, leaving out only Friday's clothes and toiletries.
- **Bring your bag to the meetings** if you can, or leave it with the hotel concierge.
- **Lisbon airport is close to the city**, about 20–30 minutes by taxi, Uber or the red metro line, but Friday evening traffic is heavy. Aim to arrive **about 2 hours before departure**, since security queues can be long.
- **Keep your liquids bag at the top** of your carry-on for security.
- **Charge your phone** and keep a power bank in your personal item.

Have a good trip!
